## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Migration crashes when `embed_category` is not set

Affected:
- db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9-16

Explanation:
`execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. On a fresh install, or on any site that never set `embed_category`, the JOIN returns zero rows. `PG::Result#[]` then raises, or returns nil and `nil['id']` raises. The migration aborts and the deploy is blocked.

The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same flaw. That setting is not always present as a row in `site_settings`, because defaults are not stored.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
rows = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")
category_id = rows.cmd_tuples > 0 ? rows[0]['id'].to_i : 0

if category_id == 0
  rows = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")
  category_id = rows.cmd_tuples > 0 ? rows[0]['value'].to_i : 0
end
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Migrated hosts are unescaped and not normalized, so existing embeds break

Affected:
- db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22-26

Explanation:
There are two problems with how existing hosts are copied over:

- **Unescaped SQL.** Each host string is interpolated directly into the SQL. A value containing `'` breaks the migration, and the pattern is SQL injection–prone.
- **No normalization.** The old setting explicitly allowed values such as `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, and entries with trailing whitespace or `\r`. These are inserted verbatim. The raw SQL bypasses the model's `before_validation` stripping.

`record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` (for example `example.com`), so any legacy entry that has a scheme, path, or trailing whitespace never matches. Existing embeds silently stop working after upgrade.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
records.map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).each do |h|
  h = h.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)}, #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input side and never matches hosts stored with a port

Affected:
- app/models/embeddable_host.rb:10-18

Explanation:
- **Case.** `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the DB column but not the incoming value. `URI("http://EvilTrout.com").host` keeps its case, so referers with uppercase letters are rejected.
- **Port.** The validation regex allows `example.com:8080`, but `uri.host` drops the port. A host stored with a port can therefore never match.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
host = uri.host
return false unless host.present?
host = "#{host}:#{uri.port}" if uri.port.present? && ![80, 443].include?(uri.port)
where("lower(host) = ? OR lower(host) = ?", host.downcase, uri.host.downcase).first
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: `before_validation` raises on nil host

Affected:
- app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8

Explanation:
`self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil. This happens with `EmbeddableHost.new`, or when the param is missing in `save_host`. The result is a 500 instead of a validation error.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
before_validation do
  if host.present?
    self.host = host.strip.sub(/^https?:\/\//, '').sub(/\/.*$/, '')
  end
end
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Admin host endpoints 500 on unknown id or missing params

Affected:
- app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-18
- app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:22-25

Explanation:
- **Unknown id.** `where(id:).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `nil.destroy`, or `nil.host=` inside `save_host`, then raises `NoMethodError`.
- **Missing params.** `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` raises when the root key is missing.
- **Unvalidated category.** `category_id` is not validated to reference an existing category. There is no FK and no model validation, so a bogus id is accepted and later used when creating topics.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
def update
  save_host(EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]))
end

def destroy
  EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id]).destroy
  render json: success_json
end

def save_host(host)
  attrs = params.require(:embeddable_host)
  host.host = attrs[:host]
  # ...
end
# model: validates :category, presence: true
~~~

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Maintainability
Title: Fabricator file contents are swapped

Affected:
- spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1-4
- spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb:1-27

Explanation:
`category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `:embeddable_host`. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works only because all fabricator files are loaded, but it is clearly a mistake and will confuse future maintainers.

Proposed fix:
Restore the category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb`. Put only the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: `_ids` hydration leaves undefined entries and assumes an array

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201

Explanation:
- **Assumes an array.** `obj[k].map` throws if a `*_ids` key holds null or a non-array.
- **Undefined entries.** `_lookupSubType` can return undefined for an unknown id. That leaves holes in the array, and `hydrated || []` never triggers because `map` always returns an array.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
if (m[2]) {
  const ids = Array.isArray(obj[k]) ? obj[k] : [];
  const hydrated = ids.map(id => self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root))
                      .filter(Boolean);
  obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated;
  delete obj[k];
}
~~~

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: `replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js:22

Explanation:
`String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. A type such as `site_customization_foo` would not be normalized. Use a global regex instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
if (ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace(/_/g, '-')) !== -1) { return "/admin/"; }
~~~

## 9) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Spec is misleading and the store test assumes behavior the mock doesn't provide

Affected:
- spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403-1405
- test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:111-117

Explanation:
- **Topic spec.** "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false. `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks hosts at all, so the test name asserts a behavior that no longer exists.
- **Store test.** `store.find('fruit', 2)` expects 2 colors, but fruit 2 has `color_ids: [3]`. The test passes only because the pretender always returns `fruits[0]`, so it is coupled to a mock quirk.

Proposed fix:
- Rename or remove the topic test so its name matches what it checks.
- In the store test, use `find('fruit', 1)`, or make the pretender return the fruit matching the requested id.

## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Client sets an undefined category after saving with no category selected

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:33-39

Explanation:
When no category is chosen, the server falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`. The client, however, sets `category` from the null `categoryId`, which yields undefined, so the row shows no badge until reload.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
host.save(props).then(() => {
  host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(host.get('category_id')));
  this.set('editToggled', false);
})
~~~
